questions.prompt: One player limps and the action is on your button with AQo at 100bb. Best default?

choices.text: Fold. A limp means the pot is already taken.
Raise larger than your normal no-limper open.
Limp behind. Never raise a limper.

questions.explanation: Isolate the limper with a stronger hand and a bigger size so you do not play a family pot.

questions.prompt: Why does the raise get bigger when more players limp?

choices.text: Each limper adds dead money you want to deny, so you add size.
Limpers are forced to fold by the rules.
The big blind shrinks after a limp.
More limpers mean you should raise smaller.

questions.explanation: A common live adjustment is your normal open plus about one extra big blind per limper.

questions.prompt: Three limpers, deep stacks, you are on the button with 22. Which is the clear mistake?

choices.text: Calling and trying to flop a set
Folding if a player then reraises very large
Folding because pairs cannot be played multiway

questions.explanation: Deep, multiway, a small pair has set value. Folding it automatically is too tight.

questions.prompt: You have KTo in middle position after two limps. What is the problem with limping behind?

choices.text: Limping is required by the rules once someone limps.
You play a dominated offsuit hand multiway and out of position against later raises.

questions.explanation: KTo is a raise-or-fold hand over limps, not a multiway limp.
